job.title: Office Manager (France) - Audio Network
job.description:
AUDIO NETWORK EST UNE SOCIÉTÉ INTERNATIONALE SPÉCIALISÉE DANS LA MUSIQUE, PROPOSANT DES CATALOGUES MUSICAUX DE CLASSE PREMIUM ET DES SOLUTIONS DE LICENCE SIMPLES POUR LES DIFFUSEURS, LES MARQUES, LES PRODUCTEURS DE FILMS ET LES CRÉATEURS DE CONTENU DANS LE MONDE ENTIER.

NOUS COLLABORONS AVEC DES COMPOSITEURS, ARTISTES ET PRODUCTEURS DE TALENT AFIN DE CRÉER UNE MUSIQUE EXCEPTIONNELLE QUI DONNE VIE AUX HISTOIRES LES PLUS INSPIRANTES.

NOTRE CULTURE REPOSE SUR LA CRÉATIVITÉ, LA COLLABORATION, L'EXCELLENCE, L'INNOVATION ET L'ENGAGEMENT À OFFRIR UN SERVICE REMARQUABLE À NOS CLIENTS.
 

L'OPPORTUNITÉ:

En tant que Office Manager, France, vous assurerez le bon fonctionnement de notre bureau parisien.Vous superviserez l'administration financière, la coordination de la paie, l'administration des ressources humaines, la gestion des prestataires ainsi que les opérations quotidiennes du bureau.

Véritable partenaire de confiance du Directeur Général et du siège international, vous contribuerez à garantir la conformité locale, l'efficacité opérationnelle et une expérience collaborateur de qualité pour notre équipe en France.

Ce poste offre une grande autonomie et requiert d'excellentes compétences organisationnelles, une attention particulière aux détails et la capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités simultanément dans un environnement international et dynamique du secteur musical.

LA MISSION:

Administration Financière

  • Coordonner les activités de comptabilité fournisseurs et clients, y compris la gestion des factures, le suivi des paiements et les relances, en partenariat avec les cabinets comptables externes et le siège.
  • Superviser les rapports mensuels de dépenses, les rapprochements bancaires et le suivi des dépenses de l'équipe.

Paie et Administration du Personnel

  • Coordonner les éléments mensuels de paie avec le cabinet comptable externe.
  • Assurer le suivi des congés et des absences.
  • Assurer l'administration des avantages sociaux des collaborateurs (titres-restaurant, mutuelle, abonnement mobilité, etc.).

Conformité Sociale et Réglementaire

  • Effectuer les déclarations obligatoires auprès des organismes compétents (URSSAF, AFDAS/OPCO).
  • Veiller au respect des obligations en matière de santé au travail et de conformité sociale.

Gestion des Fournisseurs et Contrats

  • Assurer le suivi des contrats fournisseurs.
  • Valider l'ouverture de nouveaux comptes clients.
  • Maintenir à jour la documentation administrative des fournisseurs (coordonnées bancaires, extrait Kbis, etc.).

Coordination des Parties Prenantes

  • Agir comme principal point de contact opérationnel entre le bureau de Paris, le siège international, les partenaires comptables externes, les prestataires de paie et les organismes administratifs.
  • Garantir une circulation efficace de l'information et la résolution rapide des sujets administratifs.

Gestion du Bureau de Paris

  • Assurer le bon fonctionnement quotidien du bureau (fournitures, prestataires, sécurité, accueil, maintenance).
  • Veiller à maintenir un environnement de travail professionnel, agréable et efficace pour l'ensemble des collaborateurs.

PROFIL RECHERCHÉ:

  • 3+ ans d'expérience dans un poste similaire en administration, finance, comptabilité ou gestion de bureau.
  • Expérience confirmée en comptabilité fournisseurs/clients, facturation et suivi des paiements.
  • Bonne connaissance des processus de paie et de l'administration sociale française.
  • Maîtrise des outils de gestion et de comptabilité tels que SAP et Excel.
  • Expérience dans la gestion des déclarations sociales et des relations avec les organismes administratifs.
  • Rigueur, sens de l'organisation et capacité à traiter des informations confidentielles avec discrétion.
  • Forte autonomie et excellente capacité de gestion des priorités.
  • Excellente maîtrise du français et de l'anglais, à l'écrit comme à l'oral.
  • Excellentes compétences relationnelles et aptitude à collaborer avec des interlocuteurs variés.
  • Capacité à travailler de manière autonome au sein d'une structure à taille humaine.
  • Bonne maîtrise de Microsoft Office.

POURQUOI REJOINDRE AUDIO NETWORK?

  • Rejoignez une entreprise musicale reconnue à l’échelle internationale, collaborant avec certains des plus grands diffuseurs, marques, réalisateurs et créateurs de contenu au monde.
  • Intégrez une équipe collaborative et entrepreneuriale où votre contribution a un impact direct sur l’activité et la réussite de l’entreprise.
  • Évoluez dans un environnement international aux côtés de collègues basés en Europe, en Amérique du Nord et en Asie-Pacifique.
  • Profitez d’un poste varié offrant autonomie, responsabilités et opportunités de développer votre expertise en finance, ressources humaines et opérations.
  • Contribuez à créer une expérience collaborateur exceptionnelle au sein d’une équipe passionnée et engagée.

RÉMUNÉRATION ET AVANTAGES

  • Salaire compétitif
  • Bonus annuel
  • PEE (Plan d'Épargne Entreprise)
  • PERCO (Plan d'Épargne Retraite Complémentaire)
  • Programme d'assistance aux employés
  • Titres-restaurant
  • Journées de bénévolat rémunérées
  • Horaires aménagés le vendredi durant l'été (avantage non contractuel)
  • Fermeture hivernale de l'entreprise (avantage non contractuel)

SOYEZ AUTHENTIQUE

NOTRE ENGAGEMENT EN FAVEUR DE LA DIVERSITÉ, DE L'ÉQUITÉ ET DE L'INCLUSION

Chez Audio Network, nous célébrons l'originalité, qui est au cœur de notre activité. Nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des expériences, des parcours et des perspectives contribue à créer les meilleures expériences pour tous.

Nous nous engageons à constituer des équipes diverses et inclusives dans lesquelles chacun se sent libre d'apporter sa personnalité et son authenticité au travail. Chaque collaborateur d'Audio Network est traité avec dignité, respect, bienveillance et équité.

Toutes les décisions relatives à l'emploi sont prises sans distinction de race, de couleur, de religion, de sexe, d'orientation sexuelle, d'identité ou d'expression de genre, d'origine nationale, d'âge, de situation familiale ou de toute autre caractéristique protégée par la loi. Si vous avez besoin d'un aménagement dans le cadre du processus de recrutement, merci de nous en informer afin que nous puissions garantir un processus équitable et accessible à tous.


AUDIO NETWORK IS A GLOBAL MUSIC COMPANY PROVIDING WORLD-CLASS MUSIC AND SIMPLE LICENSING SOLUTIONS FOR BROADCASTERS, BRANDS, FILMMAKERS AND CONTENT CREATORS WORLDWIDE. 

WE COLLABORATE WITH EXCEPTIONAL COMPOSERS, ARTISTS AND PRODUCERS TO CREATE OUTSTANDING MUSIC THAT HELPS TELL POWERFUL STORIES. 

OUR CULTURE IS BUILT ON CREATIVITY, COLLABORATION, QUALITY, INNOVATION AND A COMMITMENT TO DELIVERING EXCEPTIONAL SERVICE TO OUR CUSTOMERS.

THE OPPORTUNITY:

As Office Manager, France, you will play a pivotal role in supporting the success of our Paris-based business. Acting as a trusted partner to the General Manager and key stakeholders across our global organisation, you will lead the smooth delivery of finance administration, payroll coordination, HR administration, workplace operations and compliance activities.

This is a varied and highly visible role that combines operational excellence with relationship management, offering the opportunity to make a tangible impact on employee experience, business efficiency and organisational success within a dynamic international music company.

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:

  • Accounts Payable & Receivable: Coordinate accounts payable and receivable activities, including invoicing, payment processing and credit control, in partnership with external accounting providers and headquarters.
  • Financial Administration: Oversee monthly expense reporting, bank statement reconciliation, and expense control for the team.
  • Payroll & Employee Administration: Coordinate monthly payroll elements with the external accounting firm, manage leave balances, and oversee employee benefits (meal vouchers, mobility subscription, health insurance).
  • Social & Regulatory Declarations: Handle statutory declarations (URSSAF, AFDAS/OPCO) and monitor compliance with occupational health requirements.
  • Vendor & Contract Management: Track supplier contracts, validate new client account openings, and maintain supplier documentation (bank details, company registration).
  • Stakeholder Coordination: Serve as the primary operational liaison between the Paris office, global headquarters, external accounting partners, payroll providers and statutory bodies, ensuring the effective flow of information and timely resolution of administrative matters.
  • Office Supervision (Paris): Ensure the smooth day-to-day running of the Paris office (supplies, vendors, security, front-of-house), maintaining a well-organised working environment for the whole team.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING:

  • 3+ years' experience in office management, business administration, finance administration or a similar operational role.
  • Proven expertise in accounts payable/receivable, invoicing and payment follow-up.
  • Solid understanding of payroll processes and French social/labour administration.
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience working with ERP or accounting systems (SAP experience advantageous).
  • Experience handling statutory declarations (URSSAF, AFDAS/OPCO) and liaising with social organisations.
  • Rigorous and organised, with the ability to handle confidential information with discretion.
  • Strong sense of autonomy and ability to prioritise multiple tasks.
  • Fluent English and French, both written and spoken, required for daily interaction with headquarters.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Ability to work independently in a small-office environment.

Who We Are:

SiriusXM and its brands (Pandora, SiriusXM Media, AdsWizz, Simplecast, and SiriusXM Connect) are leading a new era of audio entertainment and services by delivering the most compelling subscription and ad-supported audio entertainment experience for listeners -- in the car, at home, and anywhere on the go with connected devices. Our vision is to shape the future of audio, where everyone can be effortlessly connected to the voices, stories and music they love wherever they are. 

This is the place where a diverse group of emerging talent and legends alike come to share authentic and purposeful songs, stories, sounds and insights through some of the best programming and technology in the world. Our critically-acclaimed, industry-leading audio entertainment encompasses music, sports, comedy, news, talk, live events, and podcasting. No matter their individual role, each of our employees plays a vital part in bringing SiriusXM’s vision to life every day. 

SiriusXM Media is the gateway for marketers to the largest digital audio advertising ecosystem in North America, spanning owned and operated platforms, innovative ad tech solutions powered by AdsWizz, and an extended content network reaching more than 150 million listeners each month. 

AdsWizz, a subsidiary of SiriusXM, is the leading global provider of digital audio and podcast advertising solutions, operating in over 40 countries and connecting buyers and sellers through dynamic ad insertion, advanced programmatic platforms, and innovative audio formats. 

How you’ll make an impact:

As a strategic and adaptable Staff Technical Program Manager, Ad Technology, you will own the strategy and delivery of large-scale, cross-organizational initiatives across Ads Engineering. This role is critical to driving execution of high-impact programs spanning ad-serving systems, data platforms, monetization workflows, and cross-program integrations with Pandora and broader SiriusXM systems. 

This is a senior individual contributor role requiring deep architectural literacy, systems thinking, and the ability to define program strategy — not simply execute against it. You will partner directly with engineering and product leadership to shape multi-year roadmaps, co-own program strategy, streamline org-wide governance, and deliver outcomes that materially impact platform scalability, monetization performance, and global platform capabilities to deliver outcomes that make an unmistakable enterprise-level impact across: scalability targets, RTB latency/SLA, fill rate, yield/monetization lift, reliability, and global rollout readiness. This includes leading multi-year, cross-functional programs such as global ad-serving modernization, real-time bidding (RTB) latency/scale programs, and technical consolidation across the Pandora and SiriusXM ad technology stacks.

What you’ll do:

Enterprise Program Strategy & Delivery

  • Establish and own the strategy and end-to-end delivery of large, cross-organizational Ads Engineering initiatives (eg: broadcast ads digitization and modernization, ad insertion, consolidation across SiriusXM and Pandora tech stacks), from intake through launch.

  • Function as Workstream lead for select cross-organizational initiatives spanning multiple engineering teams - from planning through launch.

  • Maintain roadmap and delivery commitments for multiple teams within the Ad Technology organization, aligning Product, Engineering and GTM on execution plans, ROIs and outcomes (e.g., latency/SLAs, yield/monetization lift, reliability, rollout readiness).

  • Coordinate program structure, milestones, sequencing, interdependencies, and success metrics in close partnership with engineering and product leadership. 

  • Proactively identify, forecast, and mitigate delivery risks and issues, communicating mitigation plans and status clearly to stakeholders.

  • Use data to drive sustainable planning and transparent tradeoff discussions for new work or conflicting priorities.

  • Provide portfolio-level visibility and structured analysis to advise on prioritization and resource allocation decisions.

  • Drive high-stakes tradeoff decisions (scope, sequencing, resourcing, risk) with Director/VP level engineering and product leadership and be directly accountable for program-level outcomes and delivery across multiple teams.

Technical Leadership & Systems Thinking

  • Apply proficient architectural literacy across ad-serving, real-time bidding, data pipelines, monetization platforms, and distributed infrastructure.

  • Guide teams toward scalable, aligned technical solutions by deeply understanding platform constraints and cross-program tradeoffs.

  • Review system designs, challenge assumptions, and proactively solve downstream impacts across tightly coupled Ads and platform integrations.

  • Manage capacity, risks, technical debt, velocity, and operational readiness.

  • Anticipate long-term platform risks and scalability constraints, including across globally distributed systems.

  • Serve as the go-to Technical Program Manager and subject matter expert for complex cross-program integrations, major platform constraints, and critical cross-domain dependency resolution.

Roadmap Alignment & Program Strategy

  • Influence roadmap alignment across Ads, Pandora, and related programs.

  • Own program-level strategy across multiple teams, including dependency mapping, sequencing, and integration planning for complex, ambiguous initiatives where outcomes and constraints evolve.

  • Co-own Ads Technology program strategy, shaping roadmap prioritization based on business impact, technical feasibility, and cross-program dependencies.

  • Advocate for program(s) health and long-term strategy.

Organizational Effectiveness & Governance

  • Define and institutionalize Ads TPM org-wide program governance standards, operating models, and best practices, elevating execution rigor across the entire Ads Engineering organization.

  • Mentor and uplevel other TPMs, and cross-functional partners by creating playbooks, templates, and coaching that improve execution quality beyond your immediate scope.

  • Continuously improve governance and delivery processes to increase predictability, execution quality, and program health over time.

  • Establish and facilitate team-level ceremonies including daily standups, sprint planning, backlog refinement, retrospectives, and/or other meetings needed to ensure smooth execution and team alignment.

  • Partner with TPM leadership to run program level ceremonies like intake and refinement if required.

  • Define, instrument, and socialize delivery and operational health metrics (e.g., predictability, cycle time, throughput, readiness, and post-launch outcomes) to drive transparent decision-making and continuous improvement.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Executive Communication

  • Build formal cross-functional networks across Product, Engineering, Data, Infrastructure, and partner programs to drive alignment and coordinated execution; influence roadmap and investment tradeoffs with senior leadership.

  • Serve as the connective layer between Engineering, Product, Quality, Operations, and external stakeholders.

  • Present clear, scenario-based decision paths to engineering and business leadership, driving consensus through clarity.

  • Resolve conflict and maintain alignment across directors, tech leads, and cross-functional partners with authority and credibility.

What you’ll need:

  • Requires a minimum of 7 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 5 years and a Master’s degree; or a PhD with 4 years experience; or equivalent experience, leading complex, enterprise-scale initiatives.

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent work experience.

  • Demonstrated experience owning Enterprise program strategy — including multi-year roadmap partnership, portfolio-level decision support, and org-wide process improvement — not just execution.

  • Significant experience in advertising technology, including ad-serving systems, real-time bidding, monetization platforms, data pipelines, and analytics systems.

  • Proficient architectural literacy across multiple platform programs; ability to guide teams toward scalable solutions and evaluate cross-program constraints and tradeoffs.

  • Executive-level communication skills; ability to craft scenario-based decision paths for senior engineering and business leadership and drive consensus through clarity.

  • Proven ability to drive delivery across tightly coupled, interdependent systems at scale. 

  • Demonstrated ability to operate with minimal oversight across ambiguous, high-stakes programs.

  • Experience working across multiple Agile methodologies; proficiency with Jira and related program management tooling.

  • Experience with automation and/or AI tools such as chatGPT, Gemini, etc.

  • Strong propensity toward relationship building and influencing without authority.

  • Experience in digital audio or media platforms preferred.

  • Experience managing vendor or third-party technology integrations, including global or multi-region platforms preferred.

  • Experience in high-availability, real-time systems environments preferred.

  • Experience leading platform transformation or cross-organizational consolidation programs preferred.

  • Must have legal right to work in the U.S.

At SiriusXM, we carefully consider a wide range of factors when determining compensation, including your background and experience. These considerations can cause your compensation to vary. We expect the base salary for this position to be in the range of $150,100 to $179,000 and will depend on your skills, qualifications, and experience. Additionally, this role might be eligible for discretionary short-term and long-term incentives. We encourage all interested candidates to apply.

job.description:

It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the role

As the Compensation Manager you will be a subject matter expert and primary resource for complex compensation analyses and program support. You will bridge the gap between analytical tasks and the strategic implementation of corporate compensation programs. You will manage specific client group relationships, lead smaller compensation projects, and provide recommendations that directly inform pay decisions and policy administration. You will be in a hybrid remote/in-office position where you will work out of our NYC headquarters 3 days per week reporting to the Vice President, Compensation and Global Mobility.

Responsibilities

  • Be a dedicated compensation partner for assigned client groups, providing in-depth analysis and consultation on compensation matters to HRBPs and business leaders.
  • Lead our recurring compensation plans, such as the annual salary survey benchmarking, maintenance of the compensation survey library, or the design and testing of compensation tools in Workday.
  • Support the annual compensation review and planning process (merit, incentive, and equity grants), including advanced data modeling, preparation of summary reports for leadership, and coordinating communication materials.
  • Conduct complex, organization-wide analysis of compensation data, including in-depth market pricing and the development of internal salary ranges.
  • Monitor compliance with applicable federal, state and local compensation laws and regulations, including the Fair Labor Standards Act, Equal Pay Act and pay-transparency requirements.

Basic Qualifications

  • 3+ years of experience in compensation or a related HR analytical field.
  • Experience conducting qualitative analysis and translating findings into clear, applicable recommendations.
  • Experience presenting analytical findings to company partners (HRBPs, Managers).
  • Solid experience with compensation management tools (e.g., MarketPay) and HRIS systems.
  • Demonstrated experience managing multiple simultaneous projects.
  • Familiarity with compensation regulations and legislation (e.g., FLSA, Pay Equity laws).
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Human Resources, or a related quantitative field.
  • Experience with Workday.

job.title: Editor, Cannonball
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is looking for an experienced, imaginative senior editor to lead Wesley Morris's weekly culture show, Cannonball, which debuted in 2025. This role is fundamentally about partnership: working closely with one of the great cultural critics of our time to keep developing the show and reaching new heights; and leading a small team of producers to translate Wesley's critical voice, instincts, and curiosity into a show that feels as engaging as it is intellectually sharp.

The show's format is loose and conversational. Episodes are built around Wesley's exchanges with fellow critics, artists, and cultural figures; at their best they feel real, incisive, intimate, surprising, loose, unpredictable and crackling with on-the-fly cultural criticism. The senior editor will play a key role in refining this format, ensuring that each episode feels cohesive, dynamic, and fun while showcasing the distinct voice and authority that define Wesley's work.

This job is for you if: you are a rigorous editor, a strong producer and an active, generative collaborator — someone who can listen as well as direct. You enjoy the give and take involved in challenging, sharpening, and expanding ideas in real time with a dynamic team. You know and have respect for Wesley's critical voice. You are an experienced and accomplished culture editor/writer/producer/thinker in your own right, someone with ideas about what's going on in the world of movies, TV, books, music, art and more. You have a keen sense of who the interesting critical voices in this landscape are, and a sense of how to program great guests each week. You are well-organized, someone capable of leading a multidisciplinary team through the many overlapping stages of development and production on multiple episodes at a time. You're adept at working within a larger editorial system, taking notes and other input. You have an understanding of YouTube and other social platforms where the show may travel. You have a feel for the right way to use audience data to inform editorial decision-making. You're adaptable, friendly, creative, and discerning. And above all, you're interested in and capable of doing all the work—both the glamorous and exciting stuff and the basic but necessary stuff—to build a successful show.

As senior editor of Cannonball, you will also be part of the staff of The New York Times Magazine, where Wesley is a staff writer and where the show is based. You will draw on and be part of the magazine's cultural coverage.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as an editorial partner to Wesley Morris, shaping episode ideas, refining arguments, and helping translate his voice and sensibility into a compelling episode.
  • Come up with interesting ideas for guests and manage the process of bringing them in and staging successful conversations with Wesley.
  • Lead the editorial process from pitch through final cut, including story development, scripting, structural editing, and post-production feedback.
  • Collaborate with producers, editors, and Magazine and Shows leadership to ensure editorial clarity, creative ambition, and high production quality across every episode.
  • Manage and mentor a multidisciplinary team, setting clear expectations, providing feedback, and fostering a collaborative, high-performing culture.
  • Oversee production timelines and workflows, ensuring deadlines are met without compromising quality or ambition.
  • Maintain a strong, consistent editorial voice while pushing the show to expand creatively and reach new audiences.
  • Develop new formats and concepts for a show that's still evolving.
  • Work with Magazine leadership to integrate the show into the Magazine's editorial plans, voice and design, helping the show grow into a recurring, high‑impact Magazine franchise.
  • Partner with audience, analytics, and platform teams to understand viewer and listener behavior and refine the show's format, distribution, and growth strategy.
  • Work cross-functionally with other newsroom desks and teams to identify opportunities for collaboration, guest booking, and editorial alignment.
  • Work proactively with Legal and Standards departments to keep the show free of corrections and/or legal challenges.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Magazine's Deputy Editor overseeing Culture.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience editing/producing cultural coverage—criticism, cultural reporting, and storytelling in a variety of formats.
  • 5+ years experience in audio and/or video production and editing, including managing soup‑to‑nuts production of long‑form, conversational shows.
  • Deep interest in movies, TV, books, music, art, and all forms of culture (both rarefied/literary and pop).
  • Sophisticated sense of how criticism can work to open up, explore and define a work of art by reading it closely, putting it in larger context, and registering a personal response to it.
  • Sharp instincts for the ways that ideas about culture intersect with everything else: politics, history, technology, identity, business, and everyday life.
  • Familiarity with digital storytelling formats.
  • Experience working with talent.
  • Highly skilled at every aspect of editing — from structuring episodes and pacing to line editing and shaping host conversations to guiding group edits and editorial brainstorms.
  • Belief in The New York Times's mission and a strong commitment to journalistic independence, fairness and accuracy.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience with a weekly publishing cadence and in managing teams under deadline.
  • 5+ years experience managing teams, including setting expectations, giving feedback and supporting people's growth.
  • Proven ability to foster an inclusive, diverse and innovative environment, both on‑air and within the team.
  • Deep familiarity with vertical video platforms and the changing social media landscape.
  • Knowledge of YouTube and social video strategy, or a demonstrated ability to learn and apply platform best practices in partnership with audience and video colleagues.
  • Experience in Adobe Premiere.

job.title: Editor, Local Newsletters
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times launched a newsletter this summer in Minneapolis-St. Paul as a pilot for a new local journalism initiative. We are now expanding to Phoenix and Nashville, and seeking an experienced, innovative editor who is rooted in one of those three cities.  

In this role, you will be the day-to-day point person for at least two of the newsletters, which will publish at least three times each week, as well as an important part of the growing Local team. You will work closely with reporters in each city to shape the tone, structure and content of the newsletters, aiming to break news and drive conversation. You will help hosts select topics of focus and frame stories; ensure that each dispatch contains a lively and engaging mix of items, including visuals; line-edit the copy and manage production;  track progress against goals; and run experiments to maximize impact.

The Local offers a blend of essential and delightful information designed to make readers more connected to their community and more conversant around the news. The newsletters will  be a bridge connecting residents of each place to the full breadth of The Times and Games, Wirecutter, NYT Cooking and The Athletic.They will showcase high-quality independent journalism from local sources, and as editor, you will help develop working partnerships with news organizations and influencers based in each area.

The newsletters help audiences understand the forces driving change around them; introduce readers to interesting characters and places they might not know; moderate and shape discussion  on public issues; curate the best relevant content from the vast digital information ecosystem; and build relationships with their audiences through callouts, social media and in-person events. 

Candidates should be deeply rooted in the Twin Cities, Phoenix or Nashville. They must have significant experience in local journalism and be committed to it as a pillar of a functioning democracy. A proven track record of engaging audiences digitally is essential; prior work on newsletters is a plus, and love for them a requirement. We’re seeking journalists with broad interests across news, politics, business, culture, sports and other beats, as well as an understanding of audience needs and the local media ecosystem. 

The editor will work remotely from one of the three cities and report in to the newsletter team . Please submit a resume, cover letter and about six work samples of any format — for example, newsletters, videos or traditional clips — that you have edited or written.

Responsibilities:

  • Edit The Local newsletter in at least two of its launch markets, including front-end story selection/shaping as well as day-to-day line-editing and production
  • Work with reporters in each market and The Local team in New York to shape the tone, structure and content of the newsletter, experimenting with story formats and other tools along the way
  • Help grow the newsletter’s audience and engagement through social media, events, callouts, partnerships and other tactics
  • Nurture relationships with local news organizations and journalists who share The Times’ values and develop new ways to partner with them  
  • Monitor the latest in how other news organizations and brands are engaging their communities and building fandom, and look for ways to leverage those ideas 
  • Help develop engagement goals and track our progress against them, using data to inform our understanding of what is working and to seed innovation and experiments
  • Represent The Local at community/media events and help plan/run our own
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • This role will report into the Deputy Editorial Director, Newsletters

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years’ experience working in digital journalism or storytelling, including some editing
  • Demonstrated superb news judgment, audience-first thinking and coverage experience across breaking news, features, analysis and enterprise
  • Experience with newsletters and social media, and a love for/commitment to both (experience in video, audio and data-journalism are a plus)
  • Fluency with analytics tools to yield actionable insights
  • Ability to identify and develop story ideas with both journalistic significance and audience resonance
  • Track record showing initiative and landing digital media projects

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • Demonstrated commitment to integrity, independence and accuracy
  • Collaborative spirit, willingness to experiment and a sense of humor
  • Deep connections to Phoenix, Nashville or Minneapolis-St. Paul
  • Omnivorous interests and a commitment to local journalism 

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

job.title: Staff Photo Editor, Digital News Desk
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

The New York Times is looking for an experienced and agile news photo editor to join our Digital News Desk team in our New York newsroom. You will help guide photographic coverage coming out of our breaking news operation, and will curate the desktop and mobile home screen presentations and our global newsletter products.

You will work closely with the editors on the Express, Newsletters, News Desks and Shows team and colleagues from photo, design, graphics and video. You will work productively, proactively and collegially with staff photographers, freelance photographers and fellow photo editors, and must be experienced and confident in working with wire services, agencies and all other sources of pictures and video, including social media and photographer estates.

In addition to driving the visual curation and presentation of The Times’ report of original assigned photography on multiple platforms, you will assign breaking news visual coverage and will be encouraged to pitch and create visual and multimedia enterprise stories. You will also contribute to Live coverage as needed. 

You have a strong demonstrable passion for photojournalism and visual storytelling of all kinds, and possess a broad knowledge of the current photographic landscape, including digitally innovative formats and mobile-first multimedia presentations. You have excellent editorial judgment and journalistic integrity and knowledge of photographic usage and copyright issues. You can edit sharply for multiple platforms, produce complex photo assignments, perform thorough agency and social media research, and work quickly and effectively in a large newsroom setting. Early mornings, nights or weekends may be required.

This is a Wednesday - Saturday position based in New York or DC and includes regular attendance in the office two days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Produce and build promotional visual assets for news stories and enterprise content with attention to detail in a fast-paced newsroom, and across a variety of digital surfaces, including the homescreen and live coverage, Listen tab and newsletters.
  • Learn, embrace and publish innovative and experimental visual storytelling formats.
  • Own critical editorial decision making in a fast-paced environment, ensuring timely and accurate visual journalism.

We’re looking for a Senior Mixed Methods UX Researcher in New York to lead this work. This is a quantitatively oriented role focused on using rigorous research and measurement to shape product and growth decisions, complemented by qualitative research when deeper user insight is needed. You’ll partner closely with product and cross-functional leaders across growth, monetization, and subscriptions, helping inform fast-moving decisions around pricing, packaging, and conversion. This role adds deep research expertise to the team. You’ll set a high bar for methodological rigor, clarify what the research can reliably answer, and guide stakeholders toward well-supported decisions. Listen to the song we made about this role! https://suno.com/s/xVPN3bUuZ4xbO8M9 What You'll Do Own survey methodology as a craft - Design and run advanced quantitative studies end to end: conjoint, MaxDiff and TURF, price sensitivity, monadic testing, segmentation, driver and key-driver analysis. Own sampling, quotas, logic, bias mitigation, weighting, and the analysis that follows. Make pricing and packaging decisions defensible - Partner directly with the PMs and leads owning subscription revenue to turn packaging, tier, and pricing questions into studies that produce an answer they can act on, with honest confidence intervals attached. Build and evolve our longitudinal measurement systems - Extend our always-on measurement program: satisfaction and sentiment trackers, product health composites, perception scales, and the reporting cadence that puts them in front of leadership every month. Make the trends trustworthy enough that people change plans because of them. Explain conversion, retention, and churn - Combine attitudinal data with behavioral data in Snowflake to answer why people convert, why they cancel, and what would bring them back. Work with data science as a peer, not a requester. Own the measurement layer of segmentation - Turn behavioral clusters into segments with attitudinal meaning: what each group is trying to do, what they value, and what they'll pay for. Keep those segments alive and validated rather than one-off. Lead qualitative work when depth beats scale - Run interviews, diary studies, and concept work to define the right constructs before you measure them, and to explain the findings the numbers can't. Advise on method selection across the org - Act as the internal consultant on when a question needs qual, quant, an experiment, or nothing at all. Push back on studies that won't change a decision. Communicate so it lands - Turn multi-source data into a clear narrative with a recommendation. Dashboards and decks are the delivery mechanism, not the output. Not "familiar with," but studies you designed and defended Experience building longitudinal measurement frameworks: trackers, benchmarks, perception scales, composite health metrics Comfortable in SQL and in Python or R for analysis, and able to work directly against a warehouse rather than waiting on a pull Fluent in the statistics that come up in practice: regression, ANOVA, hypothesis testing, and knowing when your sample can't carry the claim Proficient in qualitative methods, and clear-eyed about when the right answer is twelve interviews rather than a survey Strong product sense and an outcome-centric mindset. job.description:
Overview

Job Title: Promotions Assistant 

 

Department: Promotions

 

Reporting To: Promotions Director

 

Employment Type:    Part-Time

 

Location(s):  Richmond, VA

Work Arrangement: On-Site/Activation

 

Overview:

 

Audacy Richmond is looking for ambitious, energetic, and outgoing individuals to join our Promotions team! 

 

This is a part-time, flex schedule position with a great organization that allows you to get your foot in the door in a fast-paced, industry-leading, media company. The Promotions Assistant/Street Team position is unlike any other – this market allows the opportunity to both showcase and enhance a multitude of desired skill sets including in-field marketing, event production, live broadcast assistance, photography, videography, editing, social media coordination, office assistance and more. You'll be the face, heart, and soul of four powerful brands serving at the forefront of listener interactions, concerts, sport and lifestyle events, and much more.

 

 

Pay Transparency:

 

The anticipated starting salary range for Richmond-based individuals expressing interest in this position is $15.00/Hr..

 

Salary to be determined by the education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities and location of the applicant, as well as internal and external equity.

Audacy offers full time employees with a comprehensive benefits package to include:  health care coordinator, medical, dental, vision, telemedicine, flexible spending accounts, health savings account, disability, life insurance, critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, paid time off (sick, vacation, personal, parental, volunteer), 401(k) retirement plan, discounted employee stock purchase, student loan payment assistance program, legal assistance, life assistance program, identity theft protection, discounted home and auto insurance, and pet insurance.

 

Responsibilities

 

What You'll Do:

 

Our Promotions Assistant/Street Team is responsible for spreading the word and passion for our stations and brands to the masses by taking to the street! You will assist with everything from in-office support such as preparing and executing on-air, online, and on-site contests, contacting winners, processing winner paperwork, and more, to working live events, appearances, and remote broadcasts assisting with setup, teardown, on-site activations, audio/video equipment, driving station vehicles, and more! We are looking for energetic, dependable, flexible team members who use sound judgment and have an outgoing personality that are ready to roll up their sleeves, learn, work hard, and have fun doing it! If you love music, sports, entertainment, culture, and you have a knack for "figuring it" and "getting it done", we have a team ready to enhance and improve your skills while providing an opportunity to learn and grow in a fast-paced industry. The Promotions Assistant/Street Team is responsible for the following, including but not limited to: 

  • Execute on-site promotional events and coordinate/manage clients and listeners on-site.
  • Set up, break down, and transport promotional event equipment as required.

This role is based in Toronto (Hybrid), reporting into the People and Culture team at the CBC. 

As the Workplace Health and Well-being Advisor, you will review disability case files adjudicated by our third party provider, and coordinate employee well-being initiatives across the organization. You will partner with CBC leaders, HR and IR teams to create, maintain and enhance a workplace culture of well-being in CBC newsrooms and across the Corporation.  You will proactively monitor industry trends to guide the development and adaption of relevant policies and procedures.

At CBC/Radio-Canada:

  • Short-Term Disability (STD) and Medical Accommodation claims are administered by a third-party provider.

  • Long-Term Disability (LTD) claims are handled by CBC’s insurer.

  • Workers’ Compensation (WC) claims are managed internally.

  • Support and intervention for journalists is provided by a third party EFAP group, with additional support being provided by a Peer Support network.
     

Key responsibilities:

Supporting Disability Claims

  • Liaises with the third party/insurer for all work-related questions and complex files

  • Consults and updates CBC’s Disability Management system regarding  the status of a file

  • Responds to all HR-related inquiries sent by the third party/insurer

  • Partners with managers for any absenteeism or work-related disability issues 

  • Liaises between the third party, Manager, HR/IR when challenged (eligibility refusal, suspension of benefits, etc.) 

  • Leads and supports the return to work meetings

  • Acts as a resource to  the IR and/or legal team in grievance arbitration or litigation

  • In consultation with HR/IR and Management, requests Independent Medical Examinations (IMEs) to evaluate an employee's capacity to participate in workplace meetings or investigations, perform job duties in the absence of an open disability file, or inform decisions regarding employment termination or retirement 

  • Assists management and HR/IR in determining if accommodations recommended by the third party are possible.

Well-being

  • Supports the network of well-being champions with well-being initiatives within the workplace 

  • Participates in the development of well-being training and delivery through L&D, and also delegated through training new trainers; this includes delivery of some Hazardous and Domestic safety training, and other ad hoc training. Makes recommendations to management on programs and initiatives through the lens of journalism and media environment to ensure alignment and relevancy

  • Makes recommendations for the development and delivery of CBC News internal supports, including well-being guidelines and protocols for leadership teams, team planning sessions and debriefs connected to major difficult stories; plays a leadership and coordinating role in Peer Support network 

  • Participates as a well-being leader in manager-approved industry events and groups, including industry well-being working groups, written pieces, conference presentations, and consultations with other well-being leaders working with the CBC

  • Shares relevant well-being information through various communication channels

  • Keeps all well-being resources and documentation current and relevant

  • Drives impactful well-being initiatives, from inspiring challenges to engaging activities, promoting a culture of health and vitality.

Qualifications and Experience

  • Nursing, Healthcare, or psychology degree with experience in disability management 

  • Minimum of 7 to 10 years of experience in Disability Management, Human Resources and/or Occupational Health

  • Knowledge of federal and provincial  disability legislation and Workers’ Compensation processes

  • Proven experience navigating the healthcare industry and its unique operational challenges

  • Experience working with third-party administrators and/or insurers

  • Excellent communication skills (English), written and verbal

  • Bilingualism and/or functional knowledge of French is required

  • Demonstrated experience in designing and implementing workplace well-being and disability management programs

  • Experience working in a unionized environment is required

  • Demonstrated discretion, empathy, and professionalism in handling sensitive information.

  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

  • The ability to work independently and as part of a team, while having a customer service mindset in supporting internal stakeholders 

  • Demonstrated success collaborating with third-party administrators and insurance providers.

  • Develop and conceive photography and visual effects through framing and original camera shots to meet and anticipate program objectives as well as artistic, dramatic and other intentions.

  • Develop, design and execute lighting and sound setups, where applicable, to meet production requirements while performing shooting duties.

  • Selectively assemble images, edit, and send or save news and information program segments for future use.

  • Operate two-way radio and mapping equipment to locate and cover breaking news.
  • Review and apply technical plans and diagrams.

  • Manage disk space and storage by archiving or deleting content associated with your work as required.
  • Evaluate equipment performance as needed and draft summary reports.
  • Maintain strict quality control over all technical outputs, taking corrective action when established standards are not met.
  • Perform immediate technical repairs during equipment failures to restore service quickly, keeping relevant team members informed.
  • Attend planning or production meetings as needed.
  • Assist, as needed, in reviewing or developing operating methods and technical standards.
  • Produce technical reports by recording information relevant to your assigned work and, if applicable, entering data into designated files and applying appropriate labels.
  • Perform site surveys, as needed, to identify locations that meet production requirements.
  • Report breakdowns or defects in equipment or material to designated leads.
  • Transport staff to shooting locations according to production requirements.
  • Prepare the documentation required to transport equipment during international travel.
  • For travel outside Canada, provide the required ATA Carnet to transport equipment, check that it is complete and up to date, and ensure it is checked and cleared by customs agencies; take all necessary steps with key personnel to renew the carnet.

  • Familiarize other employees with their duties and work environment.

This role requires full-time on-site presence.

job.title: Content Sales Assistant - ANZ/APAC
job.description:
OVERVIEW OF THE COMPANY

FOX Entertainment

With a legacy spanning nearly 40 years, FOX Entertainment is one of the world’s most recognizable media brands and a leading global creator of multi-genre content across broadcast, streaming, digital and emerging platforms. Known for its independent, innovative spirit and bold storytelling, the company is committed to reaching audiences where they are through a platform- and format-agnostic approach to developing, testing and scaling intellectual property worldwide. FOX Entertainment consists of three core business units. The FOX Television Network, which encompasses its flagship linear platform and streaming partnerships with Hulu and FOX One, is home to hit series including The Simpsons, The Masked Singer, Doc, Memory of a Killer, Fear Factor: House of Fear, The Floor and Hell’s Kitchen. FOX Entertainment Studios, operates the in-house scripted and unscripted studios behind series such as Animal Control, Best Medicine, The Faithful, and The Way Home, as well as Bento Box Entertainment with animated hits such as Hazbin Hotel and Krapopolis; Studio Ramsay Global with Next Level Chef, Gordon Ramsay’s Secret Service and Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars; entertainment studio TMZ; and the independent film label Tideline. FOX Entertainment Global is the company’s worldwide content sales and distribution arm. As part of its evolution into a modern next-gen studio, FOX Entertainment is expanding its digital storytelling ecosystem with investments across vertical video with Holywater, Chain’s experiential storytelling, podcasting with Meet Cute, a two-way content pipeline with HarperCollins Publishing, and creator-led formats through the newly formed FOX Creator Studios. Through these strategic initiatives, the company is investing earlier in emerging ideas and new forms of audience engagement, while maintaining the ability to grow successful concepts into premium franchises across broadcast, streaming and global platforms. A prolific content creator and production partner, FOX Entertainment collaborates with leading studios, creators, and platforms worldwide to produce and distribute premium content at scale across broadcast, streaming, and digital ecosystems, while continuing to grow its portfolio of owned IP and next-generation storytelling formats.

JOB DESCRIPTION

FOX Entertainment Global is FOX Entertainment’s centralized content sales division, providing the worldwide multi-platform marketplace with exclusive access to its diverse, rapidly expanding production pipeline and library of owned original programming and co-production partnerships.  A central component of FOX Entertainment’s long-term growth strategy is to fortify its globally recognized, world-class brand and owned distribution platforms spanning broadcast and streaming with FOX Entertainment Global’s singular focus on broadly distributing the company’s full portfolio of owned intellectual property across all genres of scripted, unscripted and animated programming, including film and television titles as well as vertical and creator-led content.

FOX Entertainment Global is seeking a Content Sales Assistant - APAC and ANZ. The Content Sales Assistant plays a critical role in supporting the sales team across various activities and functions, including sales and account management, as well as administrative duties. The Content Sales Assistant reports to the two Directors of Content Sales APAC and ANZ and works closely with the wider Global Sales Team and other departments across the organization (Strategy & Operations, Business & Legal Affairs, Marketing, Finance, etc.) to ensure we meet and anticipate the needs of our global client base.

  • Client interactions

  • Alongside the Sales team, provides post-market follow-ups, including but not limited to screening materials and marketing information
  • Keep an accurate record of content feedback on the internal company system in a timely fashion for internal stakeholders and producers' reports
  • Track the availability of foreign language versions of FOX content (i.e., dubbed versions) for our client base
  • Proactively communicate and build collaborative relationships with cross-functional teams and external partners to ensure best-in-class customer service and business practices
  • Some travel as required
  • Perform other duties as required

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

  • 2+ years of experience in a sales, operations, or administrative role within an entertainment/media company
  • Self-starter and detail-oriented with excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills, proficient in administrative tasks, and passionate about the entertainment industry
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and time management skills
  • Strong interest and passion in media and entertainment, with the capability to learn complex industry topics quickly

job.title: Manager, Protective Intelligence
job.description:
OVERVIEW OF THE COMPANY

Fox Corporation

Under the FOX banner, we produce and distribute content through some of the world’s leading and most valued brands, including: FOX News Media, FOX Sports, FOX Entertainment, FOX Television Stations and Tubi Media Group. We empower a diverse range of creators to imagine and develop culturally significant content, while building an organization that thrives on creative ideas, operational expertise and strategic thinking.

JOB DESCRIPTION

FOX is looking for a Manager of Protective Intelligence to join their Global Intelligence team in Los Angeles, CA. As the FOX Manager of Protective Intelligence, you will detect, analyze, and assess potential and real threats to executives, talent, and all business units within the FOX Corporation umbrella. You will report to the Manager, Global Intelligence. You will be an integral part of the FOX Global Security team, directly responsible for researching, analyzing, and publishing risk assessments affecting FOX operations and productions in the US and overseas. You will leverage your deep substantive knowledge of global security and geopolitics to influence some of the company’s most complex and strategically significant decisions.  

A SNAPSHOT OF YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Research, investigate, and assess social media and open-source information to produce actionable intelligence reports, presentations, briefs, and threat assessments to protect executives, talent, and productions
  • Proactively identify, monitor, and report on imminent threats and develop training standards for GSOC Operators to assist with 24/7 threat monitoring
  • Manage, organize, and audit protective intelligence platforms in the GSOC, along with effective AI integrations; develop processes and workflows to ensure compliance with local, state, and federal data privacy laws
  • Identify and build search criteria for effective use of social media and asset monitoring platforms
  • Develop and maintain relationships with FOX Investigations, Legal, HR, InfoSec, and NYC Security Team to assist with sensitive corporate investigations
  • Research, analyze, and process open-source information to produce strategic intelligence reports, presentations, travel briefs, and security risk assessments that provide FOX Global Security with site security, protective intelligence, travel security, and global awareness
  • Identify and build search criteria for effective use of social media mining platforms
  • Support operational and tactical intelligence needs by proactively identifying emerging threats, responding to Requests for Information (RFIs) from various FOX Departments and Business Units, and publishing situational reports on imminent threats to the business
  • Respond effectively, verbally and in writing, to key departments such as EHS, HR, Corp Comms, Legal, Travel, Cyber/InfoSec, Real Estate, etc., on requests for strategic or tactical intelligence support
  • Be an active partner in the constant reevaluation of products and output to maximize efficiency and readership; engaging with customer feedback and adapting to their needs as requested
  • Develop and maintain relationships with studio intelligence partners, federal law enforcement, and other public agencies (DSAC, OSAC, InfraGard, etc.)
  • Travel as necessary to assist with major event support (FIFA World Cup, Super Bowl, etc.)

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

  • 3+ years’ experience in the intelligence field, whether private or public sector, and a deep understanding of the intelligence cycle and its application in a dynamic corporate security environment
  • Experience in the sports/ entertainment industry: broadcast, television, etc.
  • Experience with open-source intelligence tools and techniques
  • Experience with mapping and/or intelligence/information management systems 
  • Flexible schedule to support weekend, holiday, and international events, as needed
  • Deep appreciation for current domestic and global affairs, geopolitics, and history – be an avid consumer of multiple points of view and have the ability to think critically to articulate issues in a straightforward manner
  • Effective presentation and writing skills and the ability to communicate effectively (orally and written) with a variety of audiences including executives, talent, clients, and employees
  • Proven ability to accurately draw conclusions by synthesizing raw data and information from multiple, unrelated sources into a tailored, comprehensive product
  • Ability to quickly forge productive relationships and build networks at all levels, internally and externally to FOX
  • Ability to identify and solve complex problems and carry out responsibilities with little or no supervision, at times under adverse and stressful conditions
  • Ability to work independently in a dispersed virtual team structure
  • Ability to work under pressure
  • Excellent customer service and interpersonal communications skills
  • Willing to work a flexible schedule and travel, sometimes on short notice

NICE TO HAVE, BUT NOT A DEALBREAKER

  • Bachelor’s degree desirable in a field related to intelligence or global security and/or 5+ years of experience as an intelligence analyst or an equivalent combination of education and experience sufficient to perform the essential functions of the job, as determined by the company
  • Formal certifications in intelligence collection, collection management, intelligence analysis, investigations, or other intelligence disciplines from a government or professional agency

job.title: SVP, Finance Innovation
job.description:
#WeAreParamount on a mission to unleash the power of content… you in?
We’ve got the brands, we’ve got the stars, we’ve got the power to achieve our mission to entertain the planet – now all we’re missing is… YOU! Becoming a part of Paramount means joining a team of passionate people who not only recognize the power of content but also enjoy a touch of fun and uniqueness. Together, we co-create moments that matter – both for our audiences and our employees – and aim to leave a positive mark on culture.

 

Overview: 

The Senior Vice President, Finance Innovation is a newly created, high-visibility leadership role responsible for reimagining how the Finance organization operates through the application of artificial intelligence and agentic automation. This role will identify, champion, and implement AI-driven opportunities across the Finance function, with a particular focus on building agentic workflows and AI systems capable of autonomously executing multi-step financial processes with human oversight, across Accounting, Forecasting & FP&A, Treasury, Tax, and operational finance areas unique to a media and entertainment enterprise, including Production Finance and Participations & Residuals. This leader will serve as the bridge between Finance, Technology, and Data/AI teams, translating complex financial processes into scalable, intelligent automation while maintaining rigorous controls, auditability, and compliance standards appropriate for a large public company. The successful candidate will combine deep finance domain expertise with a strong point of view on emerging AI capabilities, and the organizational influence to drive adoption across a broad and often decentralized finance ecosystem. As Finance advances its Fusion systems integration, this leader will be a key voice in shaping how that effort intersects with Finance's broader innovation and automation agenda.  

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Define and lead the enterprise Finance Innovation strategy and multi-year roadmap for AI and agentic workflow adoption across all Finance sub-functions.
  • Partner with the CFO organization and Finance leadership to identify, prioritize, and business-case AI opportunities based on value creation, risk profile, and feasibility. 
  • Build and maintain a prioritized pipeline of use cases spanning close and consolidation, reconciliations, forecasting and variance analysis, cash and liquidity management, tax provision and compliance, and production finance/participations & residuals calculations and reporting.
  • Stay ahead of the external AI and finance-technology landscape (agentic frameworks, LLM-based finance copilots, RPA-to-agentic evolution) and translate relevant developments into actionable internal opportunities.
  • Partner with Product, Technology, Data & Analytics, and external delivery partners on agentic workflow and AI-tool initiatives as the Finance domain voice, defining use cases, finance requirements, and success criteria, and providing continuous feedback through design, build, and deployment. Product and Technology direct solution design, engineering, and production deployment; this role ensures what gets built reflects finance process reality and business need.
  • Own finance-side accountability across the delivery lifecycle: opportunity identification and prioritization, requirements definition, controls and change management within Finance, driving adoption, and validating realized value while Product and Technology own solution design, build, and rollout execution.
  • Specify the finance control requirements agentic systems must meet: human-in-the-loop oversight, exception handling, and escalation, and validate that the frameworks Product and Technology implement keep those systems within Finance's risk, controls, and SOX/regulatory boundaries. 
  • Convene Internal Audit, SOX, and Compliance to define the control and documentation standards AI-driven finance processes must satisfy, and carry those requirements into the Product and Technology build so solutions meet public-company standards.
  • Partner closely with the EVP of Integration on systems integration work related to Fusion, ensuring Finance requirements, controls, and adoption considerations are represented as Fusion capabilities are integrated into Finance systems and processes.
  • Accounting & Close: Identify opportunities for agentic automation in journal entries, reconciliations, close checklists, and financial reporting. 
  • Forecasting & FP&A: Champion AI-augmented forecasting, scenario modeling, and variance analysis to improve speed and accuracy of business planning.
  • Treasury: Explore agentic support for cash positioning, liquidity forecasting, bank reconciliations, and risk monitoring.
  • Tax: Identify AI applications in tax provision, compliance documentation, and regulatory research and monitoring. 
  • Production Finance: Drive automation of production cost tracking, budget-to-actual analysis, and studio/content cost reporting specific to media production.
  • Participations & Residuals: Champion agentic solutions for the complex, high-volume calculations, contract interpretation, and reporting inherent to participations and residuals processing. 
  • Serve as a visible champion and educator for AI adoption, building Finance-wide fluency and comfort with agentic tools through training, communication, and hands-on enablement.
  • Develop governance structures, including an AI use-case intake process and a Finance Innovation council or working group with representation across Finance sub-functions.
  • Partner with HR and Finance leadership to evolve talent, role design, and ways of working as agentic workflows shift the nature of finance work.
  • Manage change resistance thoughtfully, ensuring adoption is durable and supported by the broader finance organization rather than imposed top-down. Stakeholder Management & Reporting
  • Regularly report progress, value delivered, and roadmap updates to executive leadership, including the CFO and relevant Audit/Risk committees as appropriate.
  • Build strong relationships with Technology, Data/AI, Legal, business-unit finance leaders, and the EVP of Integration to ensure alignment and shared ownership of innovation initiatives, including Fusion-related systems integration work. 
  • Represent the company's Finance Innovation agenda in relevant internal forums and, where appropriate, external industry settings.

 

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or related field required; MBA, CPA, or equivalent advanced credential preferred.
  • 15+ years of progressive finance, accounting, or FP&A experience, ideally within a large, complex, public media, entertainment, or content organization. 
  • Demonstrated track record leading finance transformation, process automation, or technology-enabled change initiatives at scale. 
  • Hands-on familiarity with AI/ML concepts, generative AI, and agentic or RPA-based automation, and how they apply to financial processes; direct experience implementing such tools strongly preferred.
  • Experience with production finance and/or participations and residuals processes is a plus given the specialized nature of these areas in media and entertainment.
  • Prior exposure to SOX controls, internal audit requirements, and the governance considerations of deploying automation in a public-company financial environment. 

 

Additional Qualifications:

  • Strong finance and accounting fundamentals combined with genuine curiosity about, and fluency in, emerging AI capabilities.
  • Executive presence and the ability to influence senior stakeholders across Finance, Technology, and business units without direct authority over all of them.
  • Proven ability to translate technical AI/automation concepts into business terms finance professionals can act on, and vice versa.
  • Strong program and change management skills, with comfort operating in ambiguity and building new organizational muscle from scratch.
  • Sound judgment regarding risk, controls, and the appropriate pace and boundaries of automation in regulated financial processes.

#WeAreParamount on a mission to unleash the power of content… you in?
We've got the brands, we've got the stars, we've got the power to achieve our mission to entertain the planet. Now all we're missing is
YOU. Becoming a part of Paramount means joining a team of passionate people who not only recognize the power of content but also
enjoy a touch of fun and uniqueness. Together we co-create moments that matter, both for our audiences and our employees, and aim to
leave a positive mark on culture.


Overview
Own the product direction for one of the largest sports sites on the internet. CBSSports.com is the front door to CBS Sports for tens of millions of fans. It is where scores, live gametrackers, news, fantasy, and betting come together during the biggest moments in sports: the NFL, March Madness, The Masters, college football, Champions League, and more. This role owns the product strategy for the full web experience. You will lead a small PM team, work directly with design and engineering leads across squads, and stay close to the work. This is a player-coach role. You set the direction, and you're in the details.


Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Set product strategy for CBSSports.com and translate it into clear priorities teams can act on. Own the web plan. Decide what we're building, sequence the work, balance risk, track outcomes, and make the hard calls on what to
    continue, change, or stop.
  • Treat web as the reach and discovery engine for CBS Sports. Grow organic and direct traffic, sharpen high-intent surfaces like
    gametrackers and scores, and turn anonymous visitors into registered users.
  • Own the role web plays in the broader portfolio: growing registered users at scale and converting web audiences into sticky products
    like the CBS Sports App.
  • Prototype to think. We build working prototypes to remove ambiguity, test ideas with real fans, and learn before we commit. You'll use
    tools like Claude and Cursor to make concepts tangible, iterate on what you learn, and arrive at a better strategy because you've held
    the thing in your hand.
  • Coach and develop 1 to 2 PMs through structured feedback, calibration, and deliberate growth planning.
  • Partner with design and engineering directors on cross-squad alignment, delivery cadence, and how we evolve our process.
  • Partner with editorial to make web the place where great storytelling and great product meet.
  • Represent product to executive leadership. Turn fan behavior, competitive dynamics, and product performance into a clear narrative that builds trust.

 

How We Build (The Builder Culture)
We've moved past feature factories, PRDs, and slow-motion handoffs. We work in small, cross-functional squads with fixed timeboxes, clear ownership, and a focus on outcomes over output. When we need to figure out whether an idea works, we build a prototype and put
it in front of fans. The goal is not a finished feature. It's removing ambiguity fast enough to make better decisions. AI is how we make this possible. PMs prototype in code using tools like Claude and Cursor. Not to ship production features, but to make
ideas tangible, test them with users, and learn before we commit. Designers do the same. Engineers ship with AI as a pair programmer. We build internal tools with prompts when a workflow can be automated. This is the operating expectation, and as a Director, you'll
model it and push what's possible further. The result is that we move faster than our size suggests. Small teams, short cycles, real signals from real fans, and the autonomy to act on what you learn without waiting for permission. 

 

What success looks like:

  • The web product strategy is coherent.
  • People across the organization understand what we're building, why, and what we're choosing not
    to do. 
  • Web reliably grows reach, grows registered users, and feeds the rest of the portfolio.
  • The funnel from anonymous visitor to registered user to sticky-product user gets measurably stronger.
  • High-intent surfaces like gametrackers and scores get sharper and convert better, especially during tentpole events when traffic peaks. Ideas are tested before they're committed.
  • Teams prototype, learn from fans, and start building with real clarity.
  • Fewer false starts, less rework.
    PMs on your team grow their craft visibly and operate with stronger judgment over time.
  • Prioritization decisions are defensible, tied to measurable fan impact, and adjusted when the signal says so.
  • Stakeholders trust your perspective because you bring receipts, not just opinions.


Basic Qualifications

  • 10+ years in product, with meaningful time in a leadership role. Consumer web at scale, ideally high-traffic and real-time. You've owned the strategy, shipped against it, and developed other PMs.


Additional Qualifications

  • Strong prioritization instincts. You can hold site-level strategy and problem-level detail in the same day.
  • Fluency with the levers that move large-scale web: discovery and SEO, performance, identity and authentication, and conversion.
  • Comfort prototyping in code with AI tools. You don't need to be an engineer, but you can use Claude or Cursor to build something testable and learn from it.
  • Fluency with product analytics, experimentation, and outcome accountability.
  • An AI-native working style. You already use LLMs to think through problems and accelerate your own work, and you have a point of view
    on how AI changes what a product team can do.


CBS Sports, a year-round leader in cross-platform sports coverage, broadcasts a portfolio of events on the CBS Television Network, including THE NFL ON CBS; college football, including the Big Ten ON CBS; college basketball, including the NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship; golf, including The Masters®, PGA Championship and PGA TOUR; soccer, including the UEFA Champions League and NWSL; and CBS SPORTS SPECTACULAR. 

In addition, the division includes CBS SPORTS NETWORK, the 24-hour cable home of CBS Sports which televises live sports programming throughout the year, including college football and basketball games, UEFA Champions League and Europa League action, Italy's Serie A matches, Concacaf national team competitions, as well as a full slate of original programming and studio coverage. 

CBS Sports also delivers an extensive lineup of global soccer coverage on Paramount+, including every UEFA club competition match, all Serie A matches as well as Concacaf national team competitions, and produces INSIDE THE NFL for Paramount+. CBS Sports Digital's multi-platform offerings include CBSSports.com and the CBS Sports apps for mobile and connected TV devices; the 24/7 streaming sports news network CBS Sports HQ; 247Sports; MaxPreps; CBS Sports fantasy games; and SportsLine.
